evidence.detail: R55 RSFont calls rs/l/k repeatedly while scanning rich-text markup, using its return values to mutate current color, transparency, shadow, underline, strikethrough, tab/y-offset and inline-image state.

Direct bytecode identifies low-level tag families including pu1/pu2, fla/fla2, col, trans, shad, u, str, tab and yoff; the same class delegates glow/typewriter/text-particle/image parsing to the already-reviewed markup helpers.

R343 RichTextMarkupRegistry owns shared color/icon definitions, while rs/l/k consumes string coordinates and returns per-tag parsed control values, fixing a parser/dispatcher role rather than a registry role.
The parser owns four rs/l/i counters initialized with bounds 25, 50, 125 and 250 and uses their current values in animated/pulsing tag color calculations.

proposals.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the low-level RSFont rich-text control-tag parser/dispatcher.

evidence.detail: Each instance stores one positive bound, a current integer initialized to zero and a direction initialized to +1; tick adds direction, reverses at the upper bound and reverses again at zero.
R393 RichTextTagParser owns exactly four instances with bounds 25, 50, 125 and 250 and reads their current values for animated/pulsing rich-text controls.
Client's live update path ticks all four RichTextTagParser-owned counters every cycle before advancing its own animation timing state.

proposals.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the bounded ping-pong counters that drive RichTextTagParser animation values.
